mainTopic: Measuring on יום טוב: what 'but not with a measure' means, the honesty of אבא שאול בן בטנית, and further rules about measuring food and flour on the holiday.
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier list of the words each town used to order a portion of meat on יום טוב without naming a price. Then a new משנה teaches that you may ask a friend to fill a vessel on יום טוב, but not 'with a measure'. רבי יהודה forbids filling a measuring vessel at all. The משנה adds the story of אבא שאול בן בטנית, who filled his measures before יום טוב. The גמרא gives two readings of 'not with a measure'. שמואל says it means a vessel set aside for measuring. רבא says it means naming an amount out loud. Each reading meets the same challenge from the meat-weighing משנה, and each answers it so that רבי יהודה and the רבנן stay consistent. The גמרא then tells how אבא שאול בן בטנית and his colleagues brought wine and oil they might have gained unfairly from measuring before the Temple treasurers and refused to benefit from it, and how such goods go to צרכי רבים like public wells. It closes with more measuring rules: animal feed, spices, and רב and שמואל arguing over measuring flour for חלה. אביי's answer to the conflict over שמואל's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Local names for meat portions in different towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier list of how people in different Babylonian towns asked for a portion of meat by size, without mentioning money.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they say: 'a תרטא or half a תרטא.' In נרש they say: 'a part or half a part.' In פומבדיתא they say: 'an אוזיא or half an אוזיא.' In נהר פקוד and מתא מחסיא they say: 'a quarter or half a quarter.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line continues an earlier discussion from before this section. It lists the local words each town used to order a portion of meat on יום טוב without naming a price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may not do business in a normal weekday way, such as naming prices. So each town had its own word for a standard-sized portion. That let a person say how much meat he wanted without talking about money. The list is closing that earlier topic before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: The name used in סורא for a standard portion of meat
A part or portion (the word used in נרש)
The name used in פומבדיתא for a portion

steps.whatToRemember: Each town had its own words for portion sizes. They let people order on יום טוב without mentioning money.

phrases.english: That in Sura they say: a tarta or half a tarta.
phrases.notes: This sentence started before this section. The list is how each town asked for meat by size on יום טוב.

phrases.english: In Neresh they say: a part or half a part.
In Pumbedita they say: an uzya or half an uzya.

phrases.aramaic: בִּנְהַר פְּקוֹד וּבְמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא אָמְרִי: רִבְעָא וּפַלְגוּ רִבְעָא.
phrases.english: In Nehar Pekod and in Mata Mechasya they say: a quarter or half a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְסוּרָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a list that began before this section, about wording that avoids naming prices on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People ordered meat on יום טוב using local names for portion sizes, not prices.

steps.title: You may ask a friend to fill a vessel, but not with a measure
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: on יום טוב a person may ask a friend to fill a vessel for him, but not 'with a measure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may say to his friend, 'Fill this vessel for me,' but not with a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a basic rule. You may ask someone to fill a vessel for you on יום טוב, but there must be no measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply filling a vessel is allowed. It is not a business transaction. Measuring, though, looks like weekday selling, so 'with a measure' is forbidden. What exactly counts as 'with a measure' is not clear yet. The גמרא will ask about it later.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A person may say to his friend:
Fill this vessel for me,
but not with a measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אוֹמֵר אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב you may ask someone to fill a vessel, but not with a measure.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids filling a measuring vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that if the vessel is a measuring vessel, you may not fill it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If it was a measuring vessel, he may not fill it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a stricter view. Even simply filling is forbidden if the container is a measuring vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Filling a measuring vessel gives you an exact measurement automatically, even if nobody says 'measure.' So רבי יהודה forbids it. How far his view goes beyond the first opinion will depend on how the גמרא explains 'but not with a measure.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה כְּלִי שֶׁל מִדָּה — לֹא יְמַלְּאֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: If it was a measuring vessel, he may not fill it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter opinion than the first rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A measuring vessel may not be filled on יום טוב.

steps.title: The story of אבא שאול בן בטנית filling measures before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells about אבא שאול בן בטנית, who filled his measures on ערב יום טוב and handed them to customers on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about אבא שאול בן בטנית. He would fill his measures on ערב יום טוב and give them to his customers on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a story about a real practice. It shows a storekeeper who took care not to measure on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did all the measuring before the holiday began. On יום טוב he only handed over containers that were already full. This shows that measuring on יום טוב was something to avoid. He still managed to serve his customers.

keyTerms.meaning: A story; a case that actually happened

phrases.english: There was an incident with Abba Shaul ben Botnit,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדּוֹתָיו מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: who would fill his measures on the eve of the Festival
and give them to the customers on the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן בָּטְנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case connected to the rules about measuring on יום טוב.
steps.raayaObject: That measuring on יום טוב itself is avoided
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of אבא שאול בן בטנית, who measured everything before the holiday

steps.title: אבא שאול and the חכמים: the practice also helps on חול המועד and weekdays
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says this practice was done even on חול המועד, so the measures would be clear. The חכמים say it was done even on weekdays, so the measures would drain fully.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: He did this even on חול המועד, so the measures would be clear. And the חכמים say: He did this even on regular weekdays, so the measures would drain fully.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more opinions say the pre-filling practice was not only about יום טוב. It was also about measuring accurately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול says pre-filling gives a clearer, more exact measure, so it was done even on חול המועד. The חכמים go further: even on a regular weekday it is good practice, because it lets the liquid drain fully. Both point to honesty in measuring as a reason beyond the holiday rules.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
Making the measures clear and exact

steps.confusionAlert: This אבא שאול is a different חכם from אבא שאול בן בטנית in the story. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
He would do so even on the intermediate days of the Festival,
because of the clarity of the measures.
phrases.notes: Once the foam settles in a measure filled ahead of time, you can see exactly how much is there.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He would do so even on a weekday,
because of the draining of the measures.
phrases.notes: The liquid gets time to drip out fully, so the customer gets his full amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף בַּמּוֹעֵד עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the story and gives accuracy reasons for the practice beyond יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Filling measures ahead of time is good practice even on חול המועד, or even on weekdays, for accurate measuring.

steps.title: What does 'but not with a measure' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means by 'but not with a measure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'but not with a measure'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the meaning of an unclear phrase in the משנה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With a measure' could mean different things. It could mean saying an amount out loud, or using a certain kind of vessel. The גמרא wants a precise definition. That definition will also show how רבי יהודה's view differs from the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'but not with a measure'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אֲבָל לֹא בְּמִדָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's analysis of the first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly counts as 'with a measure' that is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: שמואל: it means a vessel set aside for measuring
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that 'not with a measure' means not with a vessel set aside for measuring. A vessel that could be used for measuring may be filled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: 'But not with a measure' means not with a vessel set aside for measuring. But a vessel that is fit for measuring may be filled.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by splitting vessels into two types. One type is set aside for measuring. The other type could be used for measuring but has not been set aside for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion in the משנה, only a vessel that is actually set aside for measuring is forbidden. A vessel that merely could measure is allowed. Using it does not look like a real measured sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel set aside for measuring
A vessel fit to be used for measuring, but not yet set aside for it

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה here, who quotes שמואל, is a later אמורא. He is not רבי יהודה, the תנא from the משנה. The next step talks about the תנא רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
But not with a vessel designated for measuring.
But a vessel that stands to be used for measuring, he may fill.
phrases.notes: He means a vessel that could serve as a measure but has not been used that way yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about what 'with a measure' means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a vessel actually set aside for measuring is forbidden. A vessel merely fit for measuring may be filled.

steps.title: So רבי יהודה forbids even a vessel fit for measuring
steps.stepSummary: Based on שמואל's explanation, רבי יהודה's point must be that even a vessel fit for measuring may not be filled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה comes to say: Even a vessel fit for measuring may not be filled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what שמואל's explanation means for רבי יהודה's opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion already forbids a vessel set aside for measuring. So רבי יהודה must be adding something new. He is stricter and forbids even a vessel that is only fit for measuring. This makes the two opinions clearly different.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the first opinion forbids only a vessel set aside for measuring. רבי יהודה forbids even a vessel that is only fit for measuring.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives each opinion in the משנה its own clear position. That is the kind of exact definition the rest of the סוגיא will build on.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda comes to say

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כְּלִי הָעוֹמֵד לְמִדָּה לֹא יְמַלְּאֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: even a vessel that stands to be used for measuring, he may not fill.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's definition to explain where רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה is stricter than the first opinion. He forbids filling even a vessel that is only fit for measuring.

steps.title: Each side seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: Based on שמואל's reading, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן lenient. But in the משנה about weighing meat, רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. So each side contradicts itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that about the joy of יום טוב, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient? But we heard the opposite from them! A משנה teaches: רבי יהודה says a person may weigh meat against a vessel or a cleaver, and the חכמים say one may not use a scale at all. There רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. So רבי יהודה contradicts himself, and the רבנן contradict themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reading. It quotes another משנה where each side seems to take the opposite position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה (as שמואל reads it), רבי יהודה forbids even a vessel that could be used for measuring, so he is the strict one. In the meat משנה, he allows weighing meat against a vessel or cleaver, while the חכמים forbid any use of a scale. So each opinion seems to flip, which creates two separate contradictions.

keyTerms.meaning: The pan of a balance scale

steps.confusionAlert: There are TWO contradictions here, not one: רבי יהודה against himself, and the רבנן against themselves. The next two steps answer them one at a time.

phrases.english: Apparently, regarding the joy of the Festival
Rabbi Yehuda is stringent
and the Rabbis are lenient?
But we heard the opposite from them!
As we learned in a משנה: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: This is the earlier משנה on 28a about selling meat on יום טוב.

phrases.english: A person may weigh meat
against a vessel or against a cleaver,
phrases.notes: He puts the meat on one side and an object he knows the weight of on the other side.

phrases.english: and the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: One may not look at the pans of a scale at all.
So apparently Rabbi Yehuda is lenient
and the Rabbis are stringent.
Rabbi Yehuda contradicts Rabbi Yehuda,
and the Rabbis contradict the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the positions that came out of שמואל's reading in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי יהודה and the רבנן as understood through שמואל's reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the meat משנה the strict and lenient roles are reversed, so each side seems to contradict itself.

steps.title: Answering the contradiction in רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The meat case uses objects that are not used for measuring. Our case is a vessel that is fit for measuring. So there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is no problem. There, it is about something that is not used for measuring. Here, it is about something that is fit for measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction by showing that רבי יהודה is talking about two different kinds of objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel or cleaver is not a measuring tool, so weighing against it is allowed. A vessel fit for measuring is close to a real measure, so רבי יהודה forbids filling it. His rule stays the same: it depends on whether the object is a measuring item.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or ready to be used for measuring

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
there, it is something not used for measuring,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the meat case, with the vessel and cleaver.

phrases.english: here, it is something fit for measuring.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by type of object)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed lenient in one place and strict in another.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is lenient with objects that are not measuring items and strict with vessels fit for measuring.

steps.title: Answering the contradiction in the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Weighing on a scale looks like weekday business, so the רבנן forbid it. Filling a vessel that is not a set measure does not look like weekday business, so they allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן against the רבנן is also no problem. There, he acts the way people do on a weekday. Here, he does not act the way people do on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction. The רבנן's rule depends on whether the act looks like a normal weekday sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a scale is exactly how meat is sold on a weekday, so the רבנן forbid it. Filling a vessel that is only fit for measuring does not look like weekday measuring, so they allow it. Their rule also stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: The way people do it on a weekday

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides stay consistent: רבי יהודה looks at whether the object is a measuring item, and the רבנן look at whether the act looks like weekday business.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult:
there, he is acting as people do on a weekday,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא לָא קָא עָבֵיד כִּדְעָבְדִין בְּחוֹל.
phrases.english: here, he is not acting as people do on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in step 9, which closes the discussion of שמואל's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (weekday manner versus not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed strict about the scale but lenient about measuring vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: They forbid only what looks like weekday business.

steps.title: רבא's different reading of 'but not with a measure'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'not with a measure' means not saying the name of a measurement. Even a vessel set aside for measuring may be filled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'but not with a measure' mean? That he should not mention the name of a measurement to him. But a vessel set aside for measuring he may fill.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second way to read the משנה, different from שמואל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the problem was the vessel itself: a real measuring vessel was forbidden. For רבא, the problem is only the words: saying a measurement amount. Because of this, רבא allows even a real measuring vessel to be filled.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a measurement (like 'one קב')
A vessel set aside for measuring

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. According to רבא, filling a real measuring vessel is allowed by the תנא קמא. Only naming the amount is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the meaning of 'but not with a measure'?
That he may not mention to him the name of a measure,
but a vessel set aside for measuring, he may fill.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מַאי אֲבָל לֹא בְּמִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 6, instead of שמואל's answer in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only saying the name of a measurement is forbidden. A vessel set aside for measuring may be filled.

steps.title: According to רבא, what רבי יהודה adds
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רבי יהודה forbids filling a vessel set aside for measuring, even without naming an amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה comes to say: a vessel set aside for measuring, he may not fill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יהודה's argument would be according to רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא, the תנא קמא allows filling a real measuring vessel. רבי יהודה is stricter and forbids it. Under שמואל (step 8), רבי יהודה forbade even a vessel that was only fit for measuring.

keyTerms.meaning: And he comes to say (this is his point)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings. For שמואל, the argument is about a vessel fit for measuring. For רבא, the argument is about a vessel set aside for measuring.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda comes to say:
a vessel set aside for measuring, he may not fill.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what רבי יהודה's view must be, based on רבא's reading in step 12, just as step 8 did for שמואל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, רבי יהודה forbids filling a vessel set aside for measuring, even without naming an amount.

steps.title: Each side seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: From the reading of the משנה, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient. But in the משנה about weighing meat, it is the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that for the joy of יום טוב, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient? But we heard them say the opposite! In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a person may weigh meat against a vessel or a cleaver, and the חכמים say you may not look at a scale at all. So רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. This is a contradiction within רבי יהודה and a contradiction within the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now raises the same challenge against רבא's reading. It points to a different משנה where the two sides seem to hold the opposite positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case רבי יהודה forbids filling a measuring vessel and the רבנן allow it. In the meat case רבי יהודה allows weighing and the רבנן forbid even using a scale. So each side looks strict in one place and lenient in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / this shows that
The joy of the festival, here meaning preparing food for it
The pan of a balance scale
There is a contradiction between one statement and another

steps.confusionAlert: The word לחומרא means 'strict' and לקולא means 'lenient.' Keep track of which side is which in each case, because the whole question comes from the switch.

phrases.english: So it seems that regarding the joy of the festival
Rabbi Yehuda is strict and the Rabbis are lenient?
But we have heard them say the opposite!
As we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: This is the earlier משנה on דף כח.

phrases.english: A person may weigh meat
against a vessel or against a cleaver,
phrases.notes: He puts the vessel or cleaver on one side of the scale, so he is not using real weights.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: One may not pay attention to the pan of a scale at all.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְקוּלָּא וְרַבָּנַן לְחוּמְרָא.
phrases.english: So it seems Rabbi Yehuda is lenient and the Rabbis are strict.
Rabbi Yehuda contradicts Rabbi Yehuda,
and the Rabbis contradict the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא גַּבֵּי שִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְחוּמְרָא וְרַבָּנַן לְקוּלָּא? וְהָא אִפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לְהוּ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same contradiction again, this time against רבא's reading in steps 12-13. Step 9 raised it against שמואל's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי יהודה and the רבנן as understood through רבא's reading (רבי יהודה forbids a vessel set aside for measuring, the רבנן allow it)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their positions in the meat-weighing משנה are reversed, so each side seems to contradict itself.

steps.title: Answering the contradiction within רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The meat case uses a vessel not meant for measuring. Our case uses a vessel set aside for measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction within רבי יהודה is not difficult. There, the vessel is not set aside for measuring. Here, it is set aside for measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the question by showing that רבי יהודה is talking about two different kinds of vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weighing against a random vessel or cleaver is not real measuring, so רבי יהודה allows it. A vessel made for measuring is a true measure, so he forbids filling it. His two rulings fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
There ... here (the other case ... our case)

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
There, it is a vessel not set aside for measuring,
here, it is set aside for measuring.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in step 14, according to רבא's reading. Here the distinction is between a vessel set aside for measuring and one that is not, rather than step 10's distinction about a vessel fit for measuring.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by type of vessel)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed lenient about weighing but strict about filling.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is strict only with a vessel set aside for measuring.

steps.title: Answering the contradiction within the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Weighing on a scale looks like weekday business. Pouring wine into a measuring vessel is something people do anyway when they drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction within the רבנן is also not difficult. There, he acts the way people act on a weekday. Here, he does not, because people often pour wine into a measuring vessel and drink from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half of the question by explaining why the רבנן forbid the scale but allow filling the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue for the רבנן is whether the action looks like weekday trade. Using a scale clearly looks like business. Filling a measuring vessel does not, since people use such vessels to serve wine at the table.

keyTerms.meaning: The way people act on a weekday

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה cares about whether the vessel is a true measure. The רבנן care about whether the action looks like weekday business. Seen this way, neither side contradicts itself.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult:
There, he is doing it the way people do on a weekday,
here, he is not doing it the way people do on a weekday,
because people usually
serve wine in a measuring vessel and drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in step 14, according to רבא's reading. It adds a reason not found in step 11: people serve wine in measuring vessels.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by whether the action looks like weekday activity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed strict about the scale but lenient about measuring vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: They forbid only what looks like weekday business. Filling a measuring vessel to serve wine does not.

steps.title: אבא שאול בן בטנית measured even on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the story from the משנה, and a ברייתא adds that he did this on חול המועד too, so he would not lose learning time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned a story about אבא שאול בן בטנית. A ברייתא taught: he did this even on חול המועד, so that he would not lose time in the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, the story of אבא שאול בן בטנית, and adds information from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, he filled his measures before יום טוב so he would not need to measure on יום טוב itself. The ברייתא adds that he did the same on חול המועד, when measuring is allowed. His reason there was different: to save his daytime hours for the בית המדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who was also a shopkeeper
חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
Losing time from learning in the study hall

phrases.english: There was an incident with Abba Shaul ben Botnit.
It was taught: he did this even on Chol HaMoed
because of losing time from the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן בָּטְנִית. תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of measuring and turns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול בן בטנית filled measures in advance even on חול המועד, so he would not take time away from learning.

steps.title: Bringing wine and oil that might not be theirs before the treasurers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that אבא שאול בן בטנית and his colleagues collected hundreds of jugs from small measuring gains and brought them to the Temple treasurers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: he collected three hundred jugs of wine from the foam of the measures, and his colleagues collected three hundred jugs of oil from the drippings left in the measures. They brought them to the Temple treasurers in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about אבא שאול בן בטנית, showing how careful he and his colleagues were about honesty in measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tiny amounts left over from measuring added up to six hundred jugs. Because these amounts might really have belonged to customers, they did not keep them. They brought them before the Temple treasurers for advice and refused to benefit from them themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: The clearing of the measures (the foam on top)

steps.whatToRemember: The story of אבא שאול בן בטנית shows two things: he valued learning time, and he was extremely careful never to keep even tiny amounts that might belong to someone else.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא כָּנַס שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי יַיִן
phrases.english: He collected three hundred jugs of wine
from the clearing of the measures,
phrases.notes: He was worried the foam on top made his customers get a little less wine than they paid for.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲבֵרָיו כָּנְסוּ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי שֶׁמֶן
phrases.english: and his colleagues collected three hundred jugs of oil
from the draining of the measures,
phrases.notes: This means the bit of oil that stayed stuck in the measure and never reached the customer.

phrases.english: and they brought them before the treasurers in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא כָּנַס שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ברייתא about אבא שאול בן בטנית, this time about his honesty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול בן בטנית and his colleagues brought the wine and oil gained from measuring before the Temple treasurers for advice, and refused to benefit from it themselves, because it might not have been rightfully theirs.

steps.title: The treasurers say it was not needed, and the donors still refuse it
steps.stepSummary: The גזברים tell the donors they did not have to bring the gains. The donors answer that they still do not want to keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The treasurers said to them: You do not need to do this. They answered: We also do not want to keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story from Step 18. The גזברים reply to the donors, and the donors reply back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזברים say the donors do not have to give the small gains away. The donors say that even if this is true, they personally do not want any benefit from it. This sets up the גזברים' practical advice in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: אִי אַתֶּם זְקוּקִים לְכָךְ.
phrases.english: They said to them: You do not need to do this.
phrases.notes: 'They' here are the Temple treasurers, answering אבא שאול בן בטנית and his friends.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: אַף אָנוּ אֵין רְצוֹנֵנוּ בְּכָךְ.
phrases.english: They said to them: We too do not want this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: אִי אַתֶּם זְקוּקִים לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא story from Step 18 with the dialogue between the donors and the treasurers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The donors were not required to give up the gains, but chose not to benefit from them.

steps.title: The treasurers advise using the wine and oil for public needs
steps.stepSummary: Since the donors want to be strict with themselves, the גזברים tell them to use the items for צרכי רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: Since you are being strict with yourselves, use them for public needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גזברים give the donors a practical solution: use the extra wine and oil for things the whole public needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donors do not want to keep the gains, but they do not know exactly whom each tiny amount came from. Using it for צרכי רבים helps everyone, so it reaches the people it came from too. The next step brings a source for this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Public needs, things that serve the whole community

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: הוֹאִיל וְהֶחְמַרְתֶּם עַל עַצְמְכֶם —
phrases.english: They said to them: Since you have been strict with yourselves,
use them for public needs.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the extra jugs of wine and oil from the measuring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: הוֹאִיל וְהֶחְמַרְתֶּם עַל עַצְמְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The treasurers answer the donors' refusal with a practical solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gains whose owners cannot be identified should be used for צרכי רבים.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a thief who does not know whom he robbed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who stole and does not know from whom should use the items for צרכי רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Someone who stole and does not know whom he stole from should use the items for public needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the treasurers' advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with someone who cannot find the person he took from. The solution is to spend it on public needs, which helps everyone, including the person he took from. The donors are in the same kind of situation, so the same solution fits.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: גָּזַל וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מִמִּי גָּזַל —
phrases.english: As it was taught: If one stole and does not know from whom he stole,
he should use them for public needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: גָּזַל וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מִמִּי גָּזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the treasurers' advice in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The advice to use the unwanted gains for צרכי רבים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a thief who does not know whom he robbed.

steps.title: What counts as public needs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly צרכי רבים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition: what kinds of things count as צרכי רבים? This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used a general phrase. To act on it, a person needs to know which projects count.

phrases.english: What are they?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a phrase in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of צרכי רבים.

steps.title: רב חסדא: wells, ditches and caves
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that צרכי רבים means public water sources: wells, ditches and caves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Wells, ditches and caves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question with examples of public projects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are places that hold water, and anyone can use them. Because everyone benefits, the person who was robbed benefits too.
steps.whatToRemember: Money or goods whose owner cannot be found go to צרכי רבים, like public water sources, so that everyone, including the owner, benefits.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Wells, ditches, and caves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בּוֹרוֹת, שִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צרכי רבים are public water sources: wells, ditches and caves.

steps.title: רבנא עוקבא's teaching: when measuring food on יום טוב is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Measuring barley exactly for an animal on יום טוב is forbidden, but roughly scooping it with a vessel is fine. A baker may measure spices so he does not ruin his food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא allowed רבנא עוקבא to teach publicly, and he taught: A person may not measure barley and give it to his animal on יום טוב. But he may scoop out a קב or two and give it to his animal without worry. And a baker may measure spices and put them in his pot so that he does not ruin his dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of measuring on יום טוב and brings a public teaching by רבנא עוקבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Careful, exact measuring looks like weekday business, so it is forbidden. Scooping roughly with a vessel, without caring about the exact amount, is allowed. A baker may measure spices because the measuring is for the cooking itself, to keep the food from being spoiled.

keyTerms.meaning: He appointed him, gave him permission (to lecture)
Scoops out a hollow from a pile

steps.confusionAlert: Using a measuring vessel is not always forbidden here. Rough scooping, where the person does not care about the exact amount, is allowed. Only careful, exact measuring for its own sake is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda appointed Rabbana Ukva,
phrases.notes: He gave him permission to give a public lecture.

phrases.english: and he taught: A person may not measure barley
and place it before his animal on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קוֹדֵר הוּא קַב אוֹ קַבִּים
phrases.english: but he may scoop out a kav or two kav
phrases.notes: קודר means digging a scoop out of the pile with the vessel, not measuring it carefully.

phrases.english: and place it before his animal, and he need not worry.
And the baker may measure spices
and put them into his pot,
so that he does not spoil his dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּנָא עוּקְבָא, וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא goes back to the halachic topic of measuring on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exact measuring of animal feed on יום טוב is forbidden. Rough scooping is allowed, and measuring spices to protect the food is allowed.

steps.title: רב: a woman may measure flour for her dough
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a woman may measure flour on יום טוב so that she can separate חלה properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: A woman may measure flour on יום טוב and put it into her dough, so that she can separate חלה generously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another measuring case, this time for a מצוה, and gives רב's lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she knows exactly how much flour is in the dough, she can separate the right amount of חלה. Because the measuring helps her do the מצוה properly, רב allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
A woman may measure flour on a Festival
and put it into her dough
so that she may separate challah generously.
phrases.notes: Literally 'with a good eye'. It means giving a full, proper amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: מוֹדֶדֶת אִשָּׁה קֶמַח בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another measuring case, this time for the מצוה of חלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב permits measuring flour on יום טוב for the sake of separating חלה properly.

steps.title: שמואל: it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and forbids measuring the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's opposing view on the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not accept the reason of separating חלה as enough to allow measuring on יום טוב. Now there is an argument between רב and שמואל, and the next step will challenge שמואל.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It is prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל forbids measuring flour on יום טוב, even for חלה.

steps.title: Challenge: שמואל's own school taught that it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: a ברייתא taught in שמואל's own school says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a teacher from the school of שמואל taught that it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling by pointing to a teaching from his own school that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is surprising for שמואל to forbid something that his own school's ברייתא allows. The גמרא now needs to explain how שמואל can hold that it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of שמואל's school taught a ברייתא

phrases.english: But didn't the school of Shmuel teach that it is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל, מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that measuring flour for חלה on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from שמואל's own school permits it, so his ruling seems to contradict his own tradition.

steps.title: אביי sets up his response to the conflict
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens by stating both sides of the problem: שמואל says measuring is forbidden, but the ברייתא from שמואל's school says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Now that שמואל said it is forbidden, and a teacher from שמואל's school taught that it is permitted,
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins answering the conflict from the last step by restating both opinions together. This line only sets up his point; his actual guidance comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not reject either source. He treats both as real, with שמואל forbidding and his school's ברייתא permitting, so his next words must tell us how to act when both opinions stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that... (opens a conclusion drawn from facts already stated)
A teacher from שמואל's study hall taught (a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי has already answered here. He is only stating the problem in full; the answer comes in the following words.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Now that Shmuel said it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's ruling from step 26: a woman may not measure flour on יום טוב for חלה.

phrases.english: and a teacher from Shmuel's school taught it is permitted,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא the גמרא used to challenge שמואל in step 27.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the קשיא of step 27 by laying out both conflicting positions before giving practical guidance.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical guidance accepting both sources (setup only in this line)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One of the two sources must be wrong, either שמואל or his school's ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי keeps both sources in view and will give guidance that takes both into account.
